pages.title: Introduction
pages.description: Jev is TypeSafe's flagship model and the first System One model. Send state and typed questions; get structured answers your code can use directly.

pages.title: Quick start
pages.description: Prefer to just dive in? Here's everything you need to get started immediately.

pages.title: Jev with coding agents
pages.description: What Jev is (and isn't) when you're using a coding agent.

pages.title: Example use cases
pages.description: Explore TypeSafe use cases by industry and turn promising ideas into software workflows.

pages.title: System One
pages.description: System One models make fast, structured decisions for software. Jev is TypeSafe's flagship model and the first System One model.

pages.title: State
pages.description: What state is, how to structure it, and how to give a System One model the context it needs.

pages.title: Primitives (Questions)
pages.description: The three TypeSafe question types (Choice, Score, Noul), the typed answers they return, how to choose between them, and how to ask several at once.

pages.title: Choice
pages.description: A Choice is a System One question type for selecting one option from a defined set. The answer includes the selected option, a probability for each option, and confidence.

pages.title: Score
pages.description: A Score is a System One question type for rating content against ordered, descriptive levels. The answer includes a score, a probability for each level, and confidence.

pages.title: Noul
pages.description: A Noul question asks the TypeSafe model to evaluate a yes/no question and return the probability that the answer is yes.

pages.title: Advanced: structure
pages.description: Instructions, Choice options, Score levels, and Noul criteria all accept JSON structure.

pages.title: Confidence
pages.description: How TypeSafe reports certainty, how it differs from probability, and how to use it to control system behavior.

pages.title: How to build with TypeSafe
pages.description: Design AI-powered software by keeping code in control and giving System One narrow, structured decisions.

pages.title: AI primer
pages.description: Why TypeSafe trains decision models with calibrated probabilities instead of optimizing for generated text.

pages.title: Patterns
pages.description: Architectural patterns for building systems with TypeSafe.

pages.title: Speculative fan-out
pages.description: Send many questions in a single call, including speculative ones, and let your code decide what's relevant.

pages.title: Confidence-gated routing
pages.description: Use confidence as a second axis. The answer tells you what; confidence tells you whether to act.

pages.title: Composite scoring
pages.description: Break a complex judgment into atomic scores, combine with weights you control in code.

pages.title: Intent routing
pages.description: Classify incoming requests and route each to the optimal handler: deterministic logic, a specialist LLM, or a human.

pages.title: Cookbooks
pages.description: End-to-end recipes that show TypeSafe in real problems, from a few questions to full pipelines.

pages.title: Self-consistency: nouls
pages.description: Route uncertain probabilities to human review while keeping the underlying noul values visible.

pages.title: Self-consistency: choices
pages.description: Add an uncertain outcome to moderation decisions and compare label agreement with the share of automatic actions.

pages.title: Parallel questions
pages.description: Runs a 13-question regulatory briefing over the GDPR Wikipedia article, showing that batching every question into one TypeSafe call is 12.2x cheaper and 10.0x faster with no change in answers.

pages.title: Re-ranking
pages.description: Builds 30-passage BM25 shortlists for 40 CLERC legal queries, then uses one TypeSafe question per query-candidate pair to raise top-1 accuracy from 5% to 18% and top-10 accuracy from 38% to 62%.

pages.title: Line-by-line search
pages.description: Build semantic search for GitHub's Terms of Service. In one request, score 218 line ids against a plain-language query with a Choice question, and use a Noul question to check whether the document contains an answer.

pages.title: Structure recovery
pages.description: Reconstructs Markdown from plain text that lost its formatting in two requests: one stitches hard-wrapped lines back together, one classifies every block (heading, list, code, callout).

pages.title: Function calling
pages.description: Turns natural-language trading requests into calls to ordinary typed functions by mapping function names and closed-set arguments to confidence-aware TypeSafe questions.

pages.title: Skill suggestion
pages.description: Picks at most one skill for an agent turn out of the 182 in Nous Research's Hermes catalog, using two TypeSafe requests to rank and re-check the top candidates.

pages.title: Knowledge graph entity alignment
pages.description: Decides which of 450 candidate pairs from two beer catalogues describe the same product using one Score question plus three companion Nouls that surface which fields disagree.

pages.title: Classifying RAG passages
pages.description: Score each retrieved passage with one TypeSafe request, then decide in code which ones reach the answering model.

pages.title: Double-checking citations
pages.description: Catch wrong or hallucinated citations by checking against the source document. One Choice question decides whether the quote's context supports the claim.

pages.title: Guardrails for LLMs
pages.description: Screen every message going into and out of an LLM app with one TypeSafe request, thresholding hazard probabilities and severity to pass, review, block, or route.

pages.title: SDE cascade
pages.description: Uses a 2-stage structured-data-extraction cascade (mini → verify → reasoning) to get most of the quality of a big reasoning model at a fraction of the cost.

pages.title: Date extraction
pages.description: Extracts absolute and relative dates by asking TypeSafe for the parts named in a document, then resolving and validating them in code with confidence-based review.

pages.title: Pre-parsed value extraction
pages.description: Uses regexes to find candidate emails, phone numbers, and amounts, then has TypeSafe select the requested span so code can normalize a verbatim value.

pages.title: Hierarchical classification
pages.description: Classifies documents through deep patent, retail product, biomedical, and source-code hierarchies using parallel beam search over TypeSafe Choice probabilities.

pages.title: Autoresearch feature discovery
pages.description: Runs an autoresearch loop that proposes TypeSafe questions, converts free text into numeric features, and uses model errors to improve a supervised CatBoost regressor.

pages.title: Classification using confidence
pages.description: Classify SEC annual reports into 75 industry groups with one Choice each, then read the answer's own confidence to decide whether to report that group or the broader division above it.
